item.description: arXiv:2606.01040v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper uses the Baire category theorem, the Riemannian manifold structure of Grassmannians, and the Khintchine Groshev theorem in Diophantine analysis, to relate properties of lattice subsets to those of associated subset of a Grassmannian.
item.dc:creator: Wayne M Lawton

item.title: On special perfect polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_2$
item.description: arXiv:2606.08640v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give some necessary conditions satisfied by special perfect polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
item.dc:creator: O. Rahavandrainy

item.title: Level totients for integer mosaics
item.description: arXiv:2606.22842v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a level analog of Euler's totient function for integer mosaics. Let $P_i(n)$ be the set of primes appearing in the first $i$ levels of the mosaic of $n$, and let $\varphi_i(n)$ count the integers $m\leq n$ for which $P_i(m)\cap P_i(n)=\varnothing$. We prove a M\"obius divisor-sum formula for $\varphi_i(n)$ and reduce it to a sum over a set $\mathcal{V}_{i,S}$ of powerful integers. If $S\neq\varnothing$, $i\geq 2$, and $q=\min S$, then \[ |\mathcal{V}_{i,S}\cap[1,x]|\sim C_{i,S}x^{1/q}, \] with $C_{i,S}$ an explicit positive Euler-product constant. For fixed $S$, the density $\delta_i(S)$ of integers whose first $i$ levels avoid $S$ exists and has an Euler product; for nonempty $S$, $i\ge2$, and $q=\min S$, the number of such integers up to $N$ is $\delta_i(S)N+O_{i,S}(N^{1/q})$. Taking $S=P_i(n)$ gives \[ \frac{\varphi_i(n)}{n}=\delta_i(P_i(n))+O_\varepsilon(n^{-1/2+\varepsilon}) \] uniformly in $n$.
item.dc:creator: The Anh Dao, Tim Kasian, Mostafa Mirabi

item.title: Superlinear complexity of the $(3/2)^n$ steering word
item.description: arXiv:2607.11648v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Write $(3/2)^n = m_n + \varepsilon_n$ with $m_n$ the nearest integer and $\varepsilon_n\in[-\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$, and let $T=(t_n)$, $t_n=2m_{n+1}-3m_n$, be the resulting \emph{steering word}: the step-by-step record of the map $x\mapsto\tfrac32 x$ on the orbit of 1, coded by nearest-integer rounding. We prove that the subword complexity $p_T(k)$ of $T$ is superlinear, $p_T(k)/k\to\infty$. A pigeonhole argument reduces this to exponential pair repulsion of the orbit modulo one, which we establish by two applications of the $p$-adic Subspace Theorem: once in three variables, which handles all gaps between the two orbit points at once, and once in two variables (Ridout's theorem) for the single degenerate family of constant gap. The argument is completely formalized in Lean~4.
item.dc:creator: Ralf Stephan

item.title: Faster Deterministic Integer Root Finding for Integer Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2608.00668v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a deterministic algorithm for finding all integer roots of a square-free polynomial $f\in\mathbb Z[x]$ of degree $n$ with $\lVert f\rVert_\infty<2^b$. The running time is $$ \tilde{O}(n^{3/2}b), $$ improving the $\tilde{O}(n^2b)$ bound of Harvey and Hittmeir (Research in Number Theory, 2022). The algorithm follows the classical $p$-adic framework: find roots modulo a prime $p$, lift them modulo a high power of $p$, and verify the lifted candidates. The main new idea is to avoid searching for a prime for which $f\bmod p$ is square-free. Instead, we find a prime for which the total multiplicity of repeated roots modulo $p$ is small. This requires lifting repeated roots, which we handle using a weighted lifting tree. We also give a faster deterministic candidate-verification algorithm: given $n$ candidate integers smaller in absolute value than $2^b$, we decide which are roots of $f$ in $$ \tilde{O}(nb+\min(n^2,nb^2)) $$ bit operations. Together, these ingredients give the first deterministic subquadratic-in-$n$ improvement for integer root finding in the square-free case.
item.dc:creator: Itamar Nir

item.title: Primitive Polynomials of the Form $g(x)+\lambda$ over Finite Fields: Non-Existence Results and Conjectures
item.description: arXiv:2608.07262v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the existence of primitive polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ whose constant term is a primitive element of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$. We prove that such polynomials do not exist if $q$ is odd, $q^n\equiv3\pmod{4}$, and the degree $m$ of the polynomial is odd. In particular, the polynomials $f(x)=g(x)+\lambda$, where $g(x)\in\mathbb{F}_q[x]$ satisfies $g(0)=0$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ is primitive, cannot be primitive under the same conditions. Further, for the cubic polynomial $x^3+x^2+x+\lambda$, we establish non-existence results in characteristics $2$ and $3$. These results, in particular, provide counterexamples to previously proposed existence conjectures. We also study the family $x^p+x+\lambda$ over $\mathbb{F}_{p^n}$. For an odd prime $p$, we prove that, provided $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(-1)^i\lambda^{p^i}\neq0$, the polynomial $x^p+x+\lambda$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{F}_{p^n}$ if and only if $n$ is even. Motivated by this result and supported by computational evidence, we formulate a conjecture concerning the existence of such primitive polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Avnish K. Sharma

item.title: Duality formulas for $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}$-multiple zeta values
item.description: arXiv:2608.12041v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce two duality formulas for $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}$-multiple zeta values ($\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}$-MZVs for short) which are defined by Takeyama and Tasaka. Since taking two different limits of $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}$-MZV recovers the $\boldsymbol{p}$-adic multiple zeta value and the $t$-adic multiple zeta value respectively, finding the relation of $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}$-MZVs partially supports the Kaneko--Zagier conjecture and its refined version. Currently, three types of duality formulas for the $\boldsymbol{p}$-adic multiple zeta values are known, and for one of them, the $q$-analogue was studied by Takeyama and Tasaka. We present $q$-analogues of the remaining two duality formulas for the $\boldsymbol{p}$-adic multiple zeta values.
item.dc:creator: Koki Ishida

item.title: Galois descents of certain multiple polylogarithms
item.description: arXiv:2608.16735v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove some conjectures of K. C. Au concerning the descents of cyclotomic levels in certain sums over multiple polylogarithms. Via answers to a question of Au in some particular cases, we also confirm Broadhurst's conjecture on honorary multiple zeta values at even weights.
item.dc:creator: Yajun Zhou

item.title: On the Diophantine Equation $p^x+ (2p+1)^y =z^2$ with Consecutive Exponents
item.description: arXiv:2608.18608v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine all positive integer solutions to $p^x+(2p+1)^y=z^2$, where $p$ is an odd prime and $|x-y|=1$. The unique solution is $(x,y,z)=(2,1,p+1)$ except when $p=7$, for which there is one additional solution, $(x,y,z)=(4,3,76)$. The proof reduces the nontrivial factorization case to an auxiliary equation, bounds its exponents using an AM--GM inequality, and isolates the exceptional solution with a divisibility argument modulo $2k^2$.
item.dc:creator: Subhasis Panda

item.title: Arithmetic purity of strong approximation for complete intersections of large dimension
item.description: arXiv:2608.27027v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove that for a smooth complete intersection $X\subset \mathbb{P}^n$ of type $(d_1,\dots,d_c)$ over a number field $k$, there exists an effective bound $N_{\mathrm{AP}}(d_1,\dots,d_c)$ such that if $n\ge N_{\mathrm{AP}}(d_1,\dots,d_c)$, then $X$ satisfies arithmetic purity of strong approximation. We establish a connecting lemma that promotes weak approximation to strong approximation under a suitable connectivity hypothesis via rational curves over $k$. We construct the required connecting conics by combining the deformation theory of rational curves with results from the circle method.
item.dc:creator: Chen Zhang

item.title: Effective Joint Equidistribution of Subspaces of Bounded Height in Rigid Adelic Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.30608v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove an effective joint equidistribution theorem for $d$-dimensional $K$-subspaces, $1\le d<n$, of a fixed $n$-dimensional rigid adelic space over a number field $K$. The parameters are the height, the image in the archimedean Grassmannian, and the isometry classes of the subspace and quotient after each is rescaled to height $1$. For bounded Lipschitz test functions, the error term is power-saving with an explicit exponent. As an application, our theorem refines Thunder's asymptotic formula for subspaces of bounded height. We also obtain a power-saving asymptotic for subspaces containing $d$ linearly independent projective points of bounded height, with a leading constant expressed as a moment of the last successive minimum.
item.dc:creator: Ruida Di

item.title: Reduced APN permutations and a disproof of the Galois-ring lifting conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2608.30808v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct infinite families of reduced almost perfect nonlinear (APN) permutations of $\mathbb{F}_{2^m}$ that admit coefficientwise permutation lifts to $\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)$ for every $k>1$. These families disprove Conjecture~2 of R\o njom and Sandrib (Cryptogr. Commun., 2026), even for reduced polynomial representatives. For every odd $m\ge5$ with $3\nmid m$, we obtain explicit seven-term polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with formal derivative identically one. We derive them from a complete criterion for the reduced representative of $A(x)^{2^s+1}$ to have no critical point in $\mathbb{F}_{2^m}$, where $A$ is an invertible linearized polynomial and $\gcd(s,m)=1$. We then apply the cube case to construct a second family of degree $2^{m-1}+2$, whose nonconstant derivatives avoid zero by an explicit trace identity. A fixed parameter in $\mathbb{F}_{32}$ gives this family in every dimension $m=5r$ with $r$ odd, including a degree-$18$ example over $\mathbb{F}_{32}$. Both constructions remain in Gold linear equivalence classes, so liftability of reduced representatives is not invariant under invertible $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear input changes. We obtain the lifting conclusions from the standard Galois-ring permutation criterion. We also verify a degree-$24$ example supplied by Zhang and Haobo, prove a trace-adjoint criterion for reduced quadratic functions, and interpret the derivative condition through ramification at rational points.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Bartoli, Pantelimon Stanica

item.title: Regular Arithmetic Functions, Volume I. Theory, Applications, Examples
item.description: arXiv:2609.09366v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This is the first of two volumes on regular arithmetic functions, and an introduction to their theory. A regular arithmetic function (RAF) is a kernel whose properties come from a single defining equation. Let $G(n,k)$ be a function of two integer variables with $G(n,n)\neq 0$, and for each $\beta$ define a sequence $(a_k)$ by $\sum_{k\le n} a_k G(n,k)=n^{-\beta}$, solved rank by rank with nothing to assume and no convergence to establish. Then $G$ is regular when the partial sums $\sum_{k\le n} a_k$ change behaviour at one exponent. Below it they reproduce the forced rate, above it they absorb it. That tipping point is the regularity index $\alpha(G)$, a quantity belonging to the kernel itself. The index came out of analogies, experiment and observation, and it is arithmetic by nature. Its most visible application is the Riemann hypothesis, which holds if and only if Ingham's kernel $G(n,k)=(k/n)\lfloor n/k\rfloor$ is a RAF of index $1/2$. It is not the only one. On a problem of a quite different kind the same theory improves the known decay bound for the orthorecursive expansion of unity. Seventeen kernels are worked out in a gallery, so that the notion can be handled by the reader. What is conjectural, conditional or open is marked as such and collected in a register. Volume II is given over to that kernel alone, with its connection to the world of Hasse-Weil zeta functions through a gauged system.
item.dc:creator: Benoit Cloitre

item.title: On an infinite family of cubic fields with explicit fundamental units
item.description: arXiv:2609.37389v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For an integer $b\neq0,1$ let $\theta$ be the unique real root of $f_b(x)=x^3-3bx-b^3$ and let $K_b=\mathbb{Q}(\theta)$. We exhibit an explicit set of $b$ of positive density for which $\eta_b=-1/(\theta-(b+1))$ is the fundamental unit of $K_b$, and we determine the set of $b$ for which $\eta_b$ is the square of a unit: it is parametrized by the Pell equation $D^2-3E^2=1$, hence infinite, and under an explicit mild condition on the field discriminant it accounts for all $b$ for which $\eta_b$ is not the fundamental unit. That condition fails for only four $b$ with $|b|\le3000$, and at one of them, $b=3$, the conclusion itself fails. In the order $\mathbb{Z}[\eta_b]$ generated by $\eta_b$, by contrast, $\eta_b$ is the fundamental unit for every $b$, so these exceptions are a phenomenon of the maximal order. As an application we construct infinitely many biquadratic fields whose $3$-class field tower has length greater than $1$.
item.dc:creator: Iwao Kimura, Hikaru Umemoto

item.title: On a question of Jones on tracelike vectors, cusp forms, and von Neumann algebras
item.description: arXiv:2609.39904v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using the theory of von Neumann algebras, Vaughan Jones showed abstractly that there is a bridge between holomorphic cusp forms and random matrices. This bridge is supplied by a distinguished function he called a {\it tracelike vector}. He posed the following problem: construct a tracelike vector to make this bridge explicit. We carry out Jones' vision for the full modular group. We construct holomorphic tracelike vectors for every finite-covolume Fuchsian group throughout the permissible Bergman range. For the modular group at the critical parameter $s=13$, we use the resulting unit tracelike vector to assign explicit group coefficients to cusp form multiplication operators, and form positive finite random matrices from a shared Haar-distributed unitary matrix. Almost surely, their normalised traces recover all joint operator moments, first as the matrix size tends to infinity, and then as the group-word cutoff tends to infinity. We also identify the limiting mixed second moment with a series of Petersson norms that involve Maass-Shimura operators of cusp forms. The exact nature of our use of AI is detailed in the introduction.
item.dc:creator: Nikolaos Diamantis, Larry Rolen

item.title: Cohomology of Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families: Newton Polytopes, Weights, and Boundary Monodromy
item.description: arXiv:2610.03081v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, $\psi$ a nontrivial additive character of $\mathbb F_p$, $\psi_q=\psi\circ\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p}$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb F_p^\times$. For $h\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n$ let $\Sigma_n(h)$ be the sum of $\psi_q(u_1^{-1}+\cdots+u_n^{-1})$ over $u\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n$ with $h_1u_1+\cdots+h_nu_n=-\lambda$, an additively twisted average of products of Kloosterman sums. For every $n\ge2$, the cohomology computing $\Sigma_n(h)$ is concentrated in one degree and has dimension $2^n-1$. It has $r(n)=2^n-\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ eigenvalues of weight $n-1$, and its other eigenvalues are the integers $q^{k-1}$, $1\le k\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$, with ballot numbers as multiplicities. The part of top weight forms a lisse sheaf $\mathcal W_n$ of rank $r(n)$ on the torus $\mathbb G_m^n$. We determine its local monodromy at the coordinate boundary and its determinant: $\det\mathcal W_n$ is the Artin--Schreier sheaf of the sum $-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}(h_1+\cdots+h_n)$ of the critical values of the phase, twisted by $p^{(n+1)r(n)/2}$. The geometric monodromy group of $\mathcal W_n$, and the arithmetic one after normalization to weight $0$, are equal to $\{g\in\mathrm{GL}_{r(n)}:\det(g)^p=1\}$. Consequently the normalized sums become equidistributed like traces of Haar-random elements of $\{g\in\mathrm U(r(n)):\det(g)^p=1\}$. The proofs use Laumon's Fourier transform, middle convolution, the Cayley cubic surface and Larsen's alternative, but no classification of finite groups.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Ebadi

item.title: Moments and Large Geometric Monodromy for Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families
item.description: arXiv:2610.04099v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $q=p^a$ with $p$ prime, $\lambda\in\mathbb F_p^\times$, and $\psi_q=\psi\circ\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p}$ for a nontrivial additive character $\psi$ of $\mathbb F_p$. For $n\ge2$ we study $\Sigma_n(h)=\sum_{u\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n,\sum_i h_i u_i=-\lambda}\psi_q(\sum_i u_i^{-1})$. On $\mathbb G_m^n$ we construct a lisse sheaf $\mathcal W_n$, pure of weight $n+1$ and rank $r(n)=2^n-\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, whose Frobenius traces equal $(-1)^{n-1}q\Sigma_n(h)$ minus an explicit polynomial in $q$, for $h\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n$. For odd $p$, its geometric monodromy has identity component $\mathrm{SL}_{r(n)}$ and cyclic component group of order divisible by $p$. The full group is $\{g:\det(g)^p=1\}$ for $n=2$, and for $n\ge3$ using boundary unipotence from the companion preprint arXiv:2610.03081. For $p=2$, the sheaf is self-dual and its geometric monodromy is $\mathrm{SO}_{r(n)}$ for odd $n$ and $\mathrm{Sp}_{r(n)}$ for even $n$. After normalization to weight zero, the arithmetic and geometric groups coincide, using the same companion input for odd $p$ and $n\ge3$. As $q\to\infty$ with $p$ fixed, we obtain Sato-Tate laws for centered, normalized sums with error $O(q^{-1/2})$ for polynomial tests and formulas for all power moments. For $p=2$, limiting moments are Gaussian through order $r(n)-1$, with an excess of one above the orthogonal value at order $r(n)$ for odd $n$; if $n+1$ is a power of two, every Frobenius on $\mathcal W_n$ has eigenvalue $q^{(n+1)/2}$. The proof uses $\sum_h|\Sigma_n(h)|^4=c_pq^{3n-2}+O(q^{3n-2-\delta(n)})$ for $n\ge3$, where $c_p=2$ for odd $p$, $c_2=3$ and $\delta(n)=\min(1,(n-2)/2)$, plane sections of the Cayley cubic, exact Frobenius-Schur identities, Laumon's local Fourier transforms and Artin-Schreier theory. For $n=2$ we identify twisted classical Kloosterman sums and compute the fourth moment exactly.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Ebadi

item.title: Cocycle Relations and Elliptic Gamma Values
item.description: arXiv:2610.10365v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent work of Bergeron-Charollois-Garc\'ia proposed a conjectural analytic expression for elliptic units for complex cubic fields as the special values of smoothed quotients of elliptic Gamma functions. These values depend on the conductor ideal, ray class group element, smoothing ideal, and an admissible element $h$. If this analytic expression is to fit into the framework of explicit class field theory, then, as in the case of torsion points on CM elliptic curves, the resulting complex number should depend only on the congruence class of $h$ modulo a fractional ideal. This conjecture has been supported by much numerical evidence. In this paper, we use the cocycle relations of the smoothed elliptic Gamma function to prove that the construction is indeed independent of $h$.
item.dc:creator: Teymour Gray

item.title: Appell Sequences in Analytic Number Theory: Shifted Expansions and Dirichlet L-Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.13565v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We place the Appell shift theorem for asymptotic expansions inside a Borel--Laplace framework and apply it to two classical functions of analytic number theory: the Hurwitz zeta function \(\zeta(m,q)\) and the Lerch transcendent \(\Phi(z,m,a)\). The resulting shifted expansions have coefficients given by Appell polynomials evaluated at the shift, with remainders controlled uniformly on compact sets. The generating sequences are identified explicitly in terms of the Taylor coefficients of the Borel kernels. In a second direction, we extend the Appell--Mellin framework of Navas, Ruiz and Varona to Dirichlet \(L\)-functions. For a primitive non-principal character \(\chi\) modulo \(q\), we construct an explicit Appell--Mellin generating function \(A_\chi(t)\) whose associated Appell sequence satisfies \(R_n^\chi(x) = L(-n,\chi,x)\), and we prove the functional equation \(A_\chi(t) = \chi(-1)A_\chi(-t)\). We further establish five structural properties of the polynomials \(R_n^\chi\): identification with generalized Bernoulli polynomials, a difference equation, an explicit formula, a Fourier expansion, and the trivial zeros of \(L(s,\chi)\). To the best of our knowledge, these results do not appear in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Abdelmejid Bayad

item.title: A lower bound for additive complements to the primes
item.description: arXiv:2610.14127v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every set $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ for which $\mathbb{P}+\mathcal{B}$ contains all sufficiently large integers satisfies $B(X)\gg\log X\log\log X$, where $B(X)=\#(\mathcal{B}\cap[0,X])$ and the implied constant is absolute. This proves a quantitative form of Ruzsa's Conjecture 2 and gives a negative answer to the $O(\log X)$ question in Erd\H{o}s Problem 32. The bound follows from a more general result: for an arbitrary set $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ and sufficiently large $X$, we construct a block of $\lfloor c\log X\log\log X/(B(X)+1)\rfloor$ consecutive integers in $[X/2,X]$ outside $\mathbb{P}+\mathcal{B}$, provided this length is positive.
item.dc:creator: Artyom Radomskii

item.title: On Solvable Automorphism Groups of Function Fields over Finite Fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.16751v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The classical Hurwitz bound gives a linear upper bound in terms of the genus for automorphism groups of algebraic function fields in characteristic zero, whereas algebraic function fields in positive characteristic can have much larger automorphism groups. Usually, one considers the case where the constant field is an algebraically closed field. Here we focus on function fields over a finite constant field. It turns out that the situation is very different. We firstly investigate solvable subgroups and $p$-subgroups of $\rm{Aut}(F/\Bbb{F}_q)$, where $p=\rm{char}(\Bbb{F}_q)$ and $F/\Bbb{F}_q$ is a function field of genus $g_F\ge2$ with full constant field $\Bbb{F}_q$. We prove that there are explicit constants $C_q^{(sol)}$ and $C_q^{(p)}$, depending only on $q$, such that, for every solvable subgroup $G\le\rm{Aut}(F/\Bbb{F}_q)$ and every $p$-subgroup $P\le\rm{Aut}(F/\Bbb{F}_q)$, $$ |G|\le C_q^{(sol)}(g_F-1),\qquad |P|\le C_q^{(p)}(g_F-1).$$ In particular, one may take $C_q^{(sol)}=12q^2(q-1)$ for $q\ge4$ and $C_q^{(p)}=5q$ for every $q$. In the second part of this article, we give asymptotic lower bounds for solvable automorphism groups. For every $q$ there is an explicit constant $L_q>0$ and a sequence of function fields $F_i/\Bbb{F}_q$ with $g_{F_i}\to\infty$, together with solvable subgroups $G_i\le\rm{Aut}(F_i/\Bbb{F}_q)$, such that $$ |G_i|\ge L_q(g_{F_i}-1) $$ for all $i$. For $q\ge5$ one may take $L_q=2q(q-1)/(q-2)$. If $q=r^2$ with $r\ge3$, an unramified tower construction over the Hermitian function field gives the stronger choice $L_q=2r^3(r-1)/(r-2)$. Moreover, as an application of our tower construction above, we improve the asymptotic lower bound of Ma and Xing for subgroups of $\rm{Aut}(F/\Bbb{F}_q)$ whose order is relatively prime to $p$. As another application, we extend our method to obtain explicit linear bounds for $p$-solvable groups in terms of the genus.
item.dc:creator: Henning Stichtenoth, Chaoping Xing, Zugan Xing

item.title: 86 unknowns for Hilbert's tenth problem over the rationals
item.description: arXiv:2610.20691v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently, Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers was solved negatively by OpenAI based on a five-contact height estimate and a pole-parity construction. In this paper, we prove further that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{86})$ with integer coefficients whether the equation $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{86})=0$ has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{86}\in\mathbb Q$.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Wei Sun

item.title: Galois Groups of Trinomials with Small Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.22764v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We calculate the Galois group of $f = x^n + ax^k + b \in \mathbb{Z}\left[ x \right]$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ for all $1 \leq \left| ab \right| \leq 3$, $n$ sufficiently large and $k$ coprime to $n$. In particular, we prove that the Galois group of $f$ is the maximal one that its factorization type allows. We do it by proving a new sufficient condition for the Galois group of a factor of a trinomial to be symmetric, which perhaps can be used to derive stronger results of this kind in the future.
item.dc:creator: Hilel Garmi

item.title: Ceresa Cycles of $X_{0}(N)$
item.description: arXiv:2501.14060v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Ceresa cycle is an algebraic 1-cycle on the Jacobian of an algebraic curve. Although it is homologically trivial, Ceresa famously proved that for a very general complex curve of genus at least 3, it is non-trivial in the Chow group. In this paper we study the Ceresa cycle attached to the complete modular curve $X_{0}(N)$ modulo rational equivalence. For prime level $p$ we give a complete description, namely we prove that if $X_{0}(p)$ is not hyperelliptic, then its Ceresa cycle is non-torsion. For general level $N$, we prove that there are finitely many $X_{0}(N)$ with torsion Ceresa cycle. Our method relies on the relationship between the vanishing of the Ceresa cycle and Chow-Heegner points on the Jacobian. We use the geometry and arithmetic of modular Jacobians to prove that such points are of infinite order and therefore deduce non-vanishing of the Ceresa cycle.
item.dc:creator: Elvira Lupoian, James Rawson

item.title: Notes on the Divisibility of Divisor Sums of Catalan Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2502.04619v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate divisibility questions for the sum-of-divisors function $\sigma(C_n)$ of the Catalan numbers $C_n=(n+1)^{-1}\binom{2n}{n}$. Using the prime factors occurring to exponent one in $C_n$, we give explicit divisors of $\sigma(C_n)$ and obtain, for each fixed integer $m\geq 2$, a power $m^{R_m(n)}$ dividing $\sigma(C_n)$, with $R_m(n)\sim\frac{2\log 2}{\varphi(m)}\frac{n}{\log n}$. We further prove uniform divisibility for all moduli up to fixed powers of $\log n$ and, with the same leading constant $2\log 2$, for almost all moduli up to $\sqrt{n}$ apart from logarithmic factors. We also establish a complete classification of the integers $m\geq 2$ for which $m\mid\sigma(mk-1)$ for every $k\geq 1$, identify precisely the exceptional coprimality relations among the associated linear forms, and record a twin-prime product divisor of $\sigma(C_n)$. The arguments use standard prime-distribution results and do not assume any conjecture concerning twin primes.
item.dc:creator: Volkan Yildiz

item.title: Semialgebraic interior layers in root closures of bounded-height integer polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2603.07397v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Finite-degree root plots of bounded-height monic integer polynomials can exhibit gaps around interior points of their root closures. Outside the closed unit disk, these closures coincide with Mandelbrot sets for affine iterated function systems with collinear digits. We construct explicit semialgebraic interior layers, certified when finite inverse orbits enter canonical self-covering parallelograms. Such parallelograms exist exactly in the non-real lens, which contains the non-real locus precisely from twenty maps onward. Within the non-real lens, limits of each capture level are captured within two additional steps, optimally, and the layers recover the locus by closure. The layers expose persistent interior deficits: explicit quadratic parameters evade every finite level; sufficiently close distinct parameters have logarithmically growing capture depths; the underlying lattice obstruction yields degree-dependent root-free radii, explaining such gaps. For non-real parameters of modulus at least the square root of the number of maps, exact enclosure trees have sharp, alphabet-independent branching bounds.
item.dc:creator: Bernat Espigule, David Juher

item.title: Extreme value theorem for geodesic flow on the quotient of the theta group
item.description: arXiv:2603.07649v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish an extreme value theorem for the geodesic flow $g_t$ on the hyperbolic surface $\Theta\backslash\mathbb{H}^2$ associated with the theta group $\Theta$. To capture excursions into both cusps of this surface, we introduce a generalized continued fraction algorithm obtained by splicing the even and odd--odd continued fraction maps into a single dynamical system. We prove that the natural extension of this map is isomorphic to the first return map of the geodesic flow on a suitable cross-section. Using spectral properties of the associated transfer operator, we derive a Galambos-type extreme value law for the digits of the spliced continued fraction. This symbolic result is then translated into a geometric extreme value theorem describing maximal cusp excursions of geodesics on $\Theta\backslash\mathbb{H}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Jaelin Kim, Seul Bee Lee, Seonhee Lim

item.title: Tiling a triangle into a prime number of congruent triangles
item.description: arXiv:2607.23453v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that if a triangle is cut into $N$ congruent triangles and $N$ is prime, then $N=2$, $N=3$, or $N\equiv 1 \pmod 4$, and every such $N$ occurs. In particular, if $N > 3$ then $N$ is not a prime congruent to $3$ modulo $4$. The argument divides into cases according to possible shapes of the tiled triangle. Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be the angles of the tile. Prior to this posting, there remained several open shapes. The two most difficult shapes were $(2\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta)$, the {\em triquadratic} shape, and $(\beta,\beta,3\alpha)$, the {\em isosceles-$\beta$} shape, in which $3\alpha+2\beta = \pi$ and $\alpha$ is not a rational multiple of $\pi$. A previous version of this paper relied on incorrect proofs of those cases, which have been retracted, and are replaced here by correct proofs. For each of those two shapes the number of tiles has the form $N = j^2 N_0$, where $N_0 > 1$ is determined by the shape of the tile and $j$ is a positive integer; so $N$ is prime, or even squarefree, only if $j = 1$. We prove by geometric reasoning that neither shape admits a tiling with $j = 1$, which shows that for both shapes $N$ is never prime, and indeed never squarefree. The shape $(\beta,\beta,3\alpha+\beta)$ (where $3\alpha + 3\beta = \pi$) has been settled by Bonfioli. In this paper, we settle the remaining cases, by number-theoretic arguments based on the area equation. Those proofs rule out $N$ prime, but not $N$ squarefree, and we give examples to show that tilings with squarefree $N$ do sometimes exist.
item.dc:creator: Michael Beeson

item.title: Recovering Laplacian Lattices from $L$-Functions of Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2608.29981v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce $L$-functions associated with characters of the Jacobian of a finite graph, as a graph-theoretic analogue of the $L$-functions arising from unramified coverings of algebraic curves. These $L$-functions are defined using the Riemann--Roch structure on the graph and extend Lorenzini's two-variable zeta function. We show that if two connected graphs without bridges have isomorphic Jacobians and their $L$-functions agree under the induced correspondence of characters, then their Laplacian lattices coincide. We also show that these $L$-functions satisfy a functional equation. Finally, we give examples showing that neither the Jacobian nor the Lorenzini zeta function alone determines the Laplacian lattice.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Labib, Antonio Lei
